**Finding submitted: deviation (LD), preferred-level cure at Subparagraph 23.2 (p0256).**

- **Investigation:** No express "liquidated damages"/"penalty" language exists anywhere (searches for liquidated damages, penalty, forfeit, damages, "shall pay an amount equal to" returned nothing responsive). The only Customer-payable machinery reviewed was 23.1/23.2 (default and capacity reclamation), 7.8 (prime-rate financial charges, capped at 120 days — compensatory, no flag), and 18.1–18.7 / p0233 (no capital-cost credit on voluntary withdrawal — left to the termination rule to avoid double-flagging).
- **Why it fails fallback:** 23.2 forfeits our reclaimed capacity without payment or credit and forfeits all amounts we have already paid, while we stay liable for unpaid accounts — an uncapped penal forfeiture triggered by a payment default roughly three months old. That exceeds any three-month early-termination-fee ceiling and is walk-away in character.
- **Redline (validated ok:true, minimality passed):** two surgical replacements inside 23.2 — "shall not be entitled to any payment or credit" → "shall be entitled to payment or credit", and the no-reimbursement sentence replaced with an unconditional bar: "No Party shall be liable for any liquidated damages or penalty under this Agreement." Every other word of 23.2, including the reclamation and unpaid-accounts mechanics, is preserved verbatim, and no retained sentence now contradicts the prohibition.
